Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.5.0

- **Hand percussion.** A new built-in model for darbuka, doumbek, bendir and similar hand drums, one drum on its own. It finds each stroke and labels it low (doum, written as a General MIDI Low Conga) or high (tek or ka, written as an Open Hi Conga). The two tones have their own colours and lanes in the piano roll and the legend. There is nothing to download, and it is covered by the app's Apache-2.0 licence, so commercial use is allowed.
- **Signal processing, not a trained model.** No open hand-drum model that allows commercial use exists, so this is not one. On two solo darbuka recordings it reads the Maksum and Saidi rhythms stroke for stroke. Velocity can be estimated from the audio's loudness, like for MuScriptor and ADTOF.
- **The drum-kit models are not for hand drums.** On darbuka recordings Drums (ADTOF) and Drums (OaF) find many strokes but label most of them as one tom, and both missed an isolated low hit. Their descriptions in the inspector now point to Hand percussion.
- **The MIDI file is easier to find.** The chip you drag into Finder or a DAW now sits in the footer, next to the zoom slider, on the Audio and MIDI editor screens. It appears once there are notes.
- **Tidier toolbar.** The Transcribe and Save buttons no longer sit inside the neighbouring pill and match the height of the other buttons. The playback position no longer leaves spare room after it.

## Known limits

- Hand percussion has been checked on two clean solo darbuka recordings only. It has not been tried on other hand drums, other players or noisy rooms. It separates two groups of strokes, low and high, so it cannot tell tek from ka, and a third tone such as a slap is labelled low or high.
- Release builds are Apple silicon only, and are not notarized.
